**Proof.**

**Fourier transform convention.** We take $\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,e^{-i\langle x,\xi\rangle}\,dx$ (the argument is identical under the $e^{-2\pi i\langle x,\xi\rangle}$ convention, since only the value at the origin and the modulus bound matter).

---

**Step 1 — Value at the origin.** Since $f \in L^1$,
$$\mathcal{F}(f)(0) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,dx = \|f\|_{L^1} = 1.$$
In particular $\sup_{\xi}|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi)| \ge 1$.

---

**Step 2 — Upper bound.** For every $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^n$, using $|e^{-i\langle x,\xi\rangle}|=1$ and the triangle inequality for integrals,
$$|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi)| = \left|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,e^{-i\langle x,\xi\rangle}\,dx\right| \le \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |f(x)|\,dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,dx = 1,$$
where the last two equalities use $f \ge 0$ (so $|f|=f$) and $\|f\|_{L^1}=1$.

Combining Steps 1 and 2,
$$\sup_{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n}|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi)| = 1,$$
and the supremum is attained at $\xi = 0$.

---

**Step 3 — Equality holds only at $\xi=0$.** Suppose $|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi_0)| = 1$ for some $\xi_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Set $g(x) = f(x)\,e^{-i\langle x,\xi_0\rangle}$, so $|g(x)| = f(x)$ and
$$\left|\int g\right| = 1 = \int |g|.$$

**Equality case of the integral triangle inequality.** For $g\in L^1$, $|\int g| = \int|g|$ holds iff there exists a constant $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ with $g(x) = e^{i\theta}|g(x)|$ for a.e. $x$. (Indeed, writing $\int g = re^{i\varphi}$ with $r = \int|g|$, equality forces $\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}g) = |g|$ a.e., hence $e^{-i\varphi}g = |g| \ge 0$ a.e.)

Applying this: there is $\theta$ such that
$$f(x)\,e^{-i\langle x,\xi_0\rangle} = e^{i\theta}\,f(x) \quad\text{a.e.},$$
i.e.
$$f(x)\bigl(e^{-i\langle x,\xi_0\rangle} - e^{i\theta}\bigr) = 0 \quad\text{a.e.}$$

Let $E = \{x : f(x) > 0\}$. Since $f\ge 0$ and $\int f = 1$, the set $E$ has **positive** Lebesgue measure. On $E$ (a.e.) we have
$$e^{-i\langle x,\xi_0\rangle} = e^{i\theta}, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \langle x,\xi_0\rangle \in -\theta + 2\pi\mathbb{Z}.$$

Thus
$$E \subseteq \bigcup_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} \bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : \langle x,\xi_0\rangle = -\theta + 2\pi k\bigr\} \quad\text{(up to a null set).}$$

If $\xi_0 \ne 0$, each set $\{x : \langle x,\xi_0\rangle = c\}$ is an affine hyperplane of codimension $1$, hence has $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure $0$. A countable union of such hyperplanes still has measure $0$. Therefore $m(E) = 0$, contradicting $\int_E f = \int f = 1 > 0$ (an $L^1$ function supported on a null set has zero integral).

Hence $\xi_0 = 0$ is the **only** point where equality holds.

---

**Conclusion.** We have shown $\sup_{\xi}|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi)| = 1$, that $|\mathcal{F}(f)(0)| = 1$, and that $|\mathcal{F}(f)(\xi)| = 1$ forces $\xi = 0$. Therefore the supremum is attained exactly at $\xi = 0$. $\blacksquare$
